items.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: finally Jack formed a band with myself and Alex Foster, a saxophone player, and Mike Richmond on bass. And we toured for a while as a band and made a couple of records for Manfred — Manfred, I say Manfred — ECM.

ctx.x: Let me do the math there.

Yeah. Well everything was so much cheaper in those days, and we used to stay at hotels that were pretty much near the clubs, a lot of them were in ghettos so they weren’t so expensive. And it didn’t really cost that much money to be on the road in those days. But I remember him telling me that, $90 a week in town, $110 on the road, pay your own hotel. So if I worked with him, when I moved to New York, that was when I moved to New York. I don’t know what he paid me in Boston, it was probably less, because I was…

at. There was a place in New Jersey called the Key Club that I played at. And so you’d start to play all these joints and then, that’s when he started paying me a little more money. And I began to become more of a professional musician. I also was out of Boston and now I was in New York. And I didn’t stay there, I went back to Boston, and it took me a couple of times to actually land in New York. Even when I met Mike and Randy I was still torn between Boston and New York. But I went on the road with this band…
